# Use your own data

## Input checklist

Your paired-end FASTQ data should meet these requirements:

- files decompress successfully;
- R1 and R2 contain equal read counts for each sample;
- the R1 suffix allows the corresponding R2 file to be inferred;
- sample names are unique;
- organism, genome FASTA, and GTF release agree;
- the STAR index was built with the matching FASTA and GTF;
- the output volume has enough space for BAM files.

## Inspect before running

```bash
iobrpy-cli map --path /absolute/path/to/fastq --json

iobrpy-cli recommend \
  --path /absolute/path/to/fastq \
  --task "Run FASTQ through the STAR workflow and retain BAM files for HLA typing" \
  --json
```

If intermediate outputs already exist, decide whether to continue downstream, rerun the current stage, or rerun the full pipeline.

## Run STAR mode

```bash
iobrpy-cli runall \
  --fastq /absolute/path/to/fastq \
  --outdir /absolute/path/to/results \
  --mode star \
  --index /absolute/path/to/star-genomeDir \
  --threads <resource_checked_threads> \
  --batch_size <resource_checked_batch_size> \
  --project MyProject
```

Run the standalone commands only when needed:

```bash
iobrpy-cli bayesprism --help
iobrpy-cli tme_cluster --help
iobrpy-cli hla_typing --help
```

Salmon mode remains available in IOBRpy for lighter expression-focused workflows, but it cannot supply the BAM files required by the HLA chapter.

## Start from TPM

If a genes-by-samples TPM matrix already exists:

```bash
iobrpy-cli tme_profile \
  --input TPM_matrix.csv \
  --output tme-results \
  --threads <resource_checked_threads>
```

Do not add `--mode` to `tme_profile`.

## Minimum research record

Record IOBRpy and external-tool versions, reference releases, index-building parameters, sample naming, thread and batch settings, the TPM-generation branch, failed samples, missing genes, and raw-data accessions. Treat nominal values and exploratory clusters separately from multiple-testing-adjusted or externally validated evidence.
